name: Museion
funding: Autonomous Province of Bolzano, plus members and exhibition sponsors.
watch: Exhibition-sponsor page not read; no Eni link found.
records_note: No annual report; the foundation's transparency portal posts annual accounts 2022 to 2025 and its six-member board, while partners appear as undated logos.

name: Centro Pecci
funding: Funded by the City of Prato and the Tuscany region.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2016 to 2024 and accounts 2016 to 2026, lists a seven-member board, and names its partners and sponsors, including PwC, undated.

name: Beppu Contemporary Art Festival
funding: Run by the BEPPU PROJECT NPO with the city.
watch: Last full festival was in 2015. Oita Gas, a natural-gas utility, is a current sponsor. No protest was found; the exclusion comes from the fossil-fuel rule alone.
why_flagged: Last full festival was in 2015. Oita Gas, a natural-gas utility, is a current sponsor. No protest was found; the exclusion comes from the fossil-fuel rule alone.
records_note: Beppu Project posts festival reports for 2012 to 2014 with income and spending, a named 2025 sponsor list of about 30, and no board.

name: Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: FY2024 report: City of Hiroshima, plus grants from the Agency for Cultural Affairs, Ogasawara Foundation and Asahi Shimbun Foundation.
watch: Municipal museum; roster not checked. Chim↑Pom solo show cancelled after their Oct 2008 'Pika' skywriting over Hiroshima drew public backlash. 2026 Mel Chin show co-run with Asahi Shimbun.
records_note: The city museum posts yearly reports for FY2017 to FY2024 that credit funders per show, but shows no accounts and no board list.
sources: https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/?i=Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art (Hiroshima MOCA)

name: Okayama Art Summit
funding: Okayama City, Okayama Prefecture and the Ishikawa Foundation lead the executive committee. Stripe International and Chugoku Bank are corporate partners. Foundation president Yasuharu Ishikawa directs the Summit.
watch: Citizens petitioned the city council and prefecture in 2021 and 2022 over harassment allegations against Ishikawa. Both were rejected; he directs the 2025 edition.
records_note: The 2025 summit site names its executive committee, sponsors and supporting agencies by name, but posts no reports or accounts.

name: Sapporo International Art Festival
funding: SIAF2027 is organised by the City of Sapporo's executive committee, supported by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, the Kao Foundation and partners including Wacom.
watch: Municipal festival; roster not checked. Kao Foundation (consumer goods) and Wacom (electronics) are the named corporate money.
records_note: Sapporo's city site posts the festival committee's reports and settled accounts for FY2020 to FY2024, its member roster of May 2025, and named partners.

name: Setouchi Triennale
funding: Executive committee led by Kagawa Prefecture and the Fukutake Foundation. Sponsors (Feb 2025): Japan Tobacco, Cosmo Oil, Okayama Gas, Shikoku Electric Power, Chari-Loto, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Mitsui & Co.
watch: Chari-Loto sells online keirin race bets. Okayama Gas is a gas utility and Cosmo Oil a refiner. Japan Tobacco is a tobacco maker.
records_note: The festival lists over 200 sponsors and donors as of February 2025 and names its executive committee, but posts no reports or accounts.

name: Echigo-Tsumari Art Triennale
funding: 2024: JPY 360M committee budget and 545,931 visits. Paid for by Tokamachi/Tsunan, Agency for Cultural Affairs/JAC, tickets and furusato-nozei gifts.
watch: Corporate sponsor list not read. TEPCO Niigata (Fukushima operator) is a corporate supporter, giving staff and a venue in kind. The report does not name its 30 corporate donors (JPY 21M).
records_note: The committee posts summary reports for 2018, 2022 and 2024 with accounts and officers, and the support page names sponsors without a date.

name: Artizon Museum
funding: Run by the Ishibashi Foundation, set up in 1956 by Bridgestone founder Shojiro Ishibashi, who gave it his art collection. Known as the Bridgestone Museum of Art before.
watch: Bridgestone's Firestone unit was sued in 2005 over child labour on its Liberian plantation; the Seventh Circuit ruled for Firestone in 2011.
records_note: The Ishibashi Foundation, Artizon's operator, posts reports from 2019, balance sheets for 2020 to 2025 and a dated officer list, but no donor list.

name: Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media (YCAM)
funding: FY2021 programme budget ¥305M: 88.7% Yamaguchi City, 3.3% Agency for Cultural Affairs grants. The 2026 show is funded by the same two.
watch: Municipal media-art centre; roster not checked. The latest published budget breakdown is FY2021. Corporate links are commissioned R&D only (Sony CSL, Mitsukoshi Isetan). No controversy found.
records_note: YCAM posts annual reports for FY2009 to FY2021 with a programme outturn table, but no funder list and no named board.

name: Makan Art Space
funding: Founded 2003; rentals and screenings, then grants from AFAC and SIDA.
watch: Artist-run; unclear whether it still operates.
records_note: Makan's old website is gone and no reports, accounts, funders or board are posted anywhere found.

name: MO Museum
funding: Private museum founded by Danguolė and Viktoras Butkus (biotech).
records_note: MO posts annual reports for 2018-19 to 2025, names its patrons and partners on an undated page, and lists an advisory board, but no accounts.
